title: Disable export.git-add and require bd dolt push in runner workflow
description:
Two coupled fixes to unblock autonomous Jules dispatches end-to-end:

## Fix 1 — bd config: export.git-add = false

bd's auto-export (export.auto=true, set in sm-w8bo) runs 'git add .beads/issues.jsonl' after every bd write. After sm-qtsp removed issues.jsonl from .beads/.gitignore, the git add now succeeds and leaves a staged change — Jules's env_setup verification halts on the dirty tree.

Set via 'bd config set export.git-add false'. Keeps export.auto=true (still useful for local viewer / snapshot) but no longer dirties the working tree.

## Fix 2 — delegation-contract.md + delegation-template.md: require 'bd dolt push' at end of runner workflow

Today's 5 research-readonly dispatches all completed but stranded the deliverable in Jules's sandbox: Jules ran 'bd update --claim', 'bd comment', 'bd close' — but never 'bd dolt push', so none of it propagated back. The contract currently tells the runner to use bd CLI as the output channel for research-readonly beads, but never says to push bd state. Invisible gap for impl beads (the PR via 'git push' carries them) and fatal for research-readonly.

Add a final mandatory step to the runner workflow in delegation-contract.md AND the completion checkboxes in delegation-template.md: 'bd dolt push' MUST be the runner's last action before reporting done.

## Path allowlist

git add allowed for:
  - .beads/config.yaml (via 'bd config set', not hand edit)
  - .jules/prompts/delegation-contract.md
  - .jules/prompts/delegation-template.md
acceptance_criteria: Given the bd config change committed and the contract/template updated, when a fresh Jules env_setup completes, then 'git status --porcelain' prints nothing; and when a research-readonly bead is re-dispatched, then after session COMPLETED the bead shows a delegate-output comment and CLOSED status without manual intervention

<!-- delegate-output -->

## Sketch / Feature / Unit (cabinet) references in assembly aggregates

Scanned `packages/assembly/src/Project.ts`, `Assembly.ts`, `SpaceInstance.ts` (entire files read, not just grep). Symbols searched: `Sketch2D`, `SketchElement`, `SketchElementId`, `SketchId`, `SketchFeature`, `SketchLine`, `SketchRectangle`, `Feature`, `Unit` (cabinet domain).

### Project.ts (18 lines)

- Imports: `AssemblySchema` from `./Assembly` only.
- Fields: `id`, `name`, `assemblies`, `budgetCap`, `notes`.
- Sketch references: **none**.
- Feature references: **none**.
- Unit (cabinet) references: **none** — only transitive via `assemblies` → `Assembly`.

### Assembly.ts (28 lines)

- Imports: `UnitSchema` from `./Unit` (the cabinet domain object), `SpaceInstanceSchema`, `AggregateConstraintSchema`, `StorageCategorySchema`, `BinSpecIdSchema`.
- Fields: `id`, `name`, `units` (array of `UnitSchema`), `standaloneSpaces`, `aggregateConstraints`, `globalLimits`, `storageCategories`.
- Sketch references: **none**.
- Feature references: **none**.
- Unit (cabinet) references: **direct** — `units` field is `z.array(UnitSchema)`, line 17. Import at line 2.

### SpaceInstance.ts (23 lines)

- Imports: `SpaceTemplateIdSchema`, `SpaceConstraintSchema`, `PlacedBinSchema`, `PackingStrategyIdSchema`, `BinSpecIdSchema`.
- Fields: `id`, `templateId`, `name`, `count`, `constraints`, `activeStrategy`, `placedBins`.
- Sketch references: **none**.
- Feature references: **none**.
- Unit (cabinet) references: **none**.

### Decision impact for slice 2

- `Project` and `SpaceInstance`: clean. No sketch refs to strip, no Unit coupling. Can stay as-is or be deleted on independent grounds.
- `Assembly`: has a hard dependency on `Unit` (cabinet) via the `units: z.array(UnitSchema)` field. Removing `Unit` (sm-eh3y) requires either (a) deleting `Assembly.units` and the file's import, or (b) deleting `Assembly` itself. Sketch-stripping is a no-op for `Assembly` because no sketch refs exist.

**Conclusion**: there are no sketch references in any of the three aggregates. The earlier "sketch refs stripped" framing in the bead description was a false premise. The slice-2 decision reduces to whether `Unit` (cabinet) is deleted (sm-eh3y) and how `Assembly.units` is handled in its absence.

title: CI verify fails: vitest workers crash under Bun runtime when web tests import zod
description:
Root 'bun run test' ran vitest with [run] bun = true shimming node to Bun; zod's ESM named exports resolve undefined under Bun, so any unmocked catalog/assembly import in web vitest tests crashes (surfaced by GoldenPathSetup in PR #141).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Keep [run] bun = true in bunfig.toml.
2. Add a web vitest test that imports @storagemaxxing/catalog (zod) without mocking.
3. Run 'bun run test' at the repo root.
4. Observe: TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'z.string') at packages/catalog/src/bin.ts.

Fix: remove [run] bun = true from bunfig.toml, delegate root web tests via 'bun run --filter @storagemaxxing/web test', make apps/web test script non-watch ('vitest run'), and document the caveat in AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fresh install, when 'bun run test' runs at the repo root, then package and web vitest suites pass, including tests that import catalog modules using zod.
close_reason: Removed [run] bun = true, root test delegates via --filter, AGENTS.md documents the caveat; all gates green locally

title: Silence env_setup harmless noise warnings
description:
env_setup.sh emits two harmless but noisy warnings on every Jules session:

1. 'Warning: /app/.beads has permissions 0775 (recommended: 0700). Run: chmod 700 /app/.beads'
2. 'Warning: auto-export: git add failed ... .beads/issues.jsonl ignored by .gitignore'

Both have canonical fixes pinned below — runner does not negotiate.

## Fix 1 (permissions)

Append a single command after the existing bd dolt pull line in .jules/env_setup.sh:

    chmod 700 .beads

Run AFTER bd commands (so bd has finished writing) and BEFORE the script exits.

## Fix 2 (auto-export gitignore)

Remove the line 'issues.jsonl' from .beads/.gitignore. With export.auto=true (committed in sm-w8bo), bd auto-exports issue state to .beads/issues.jsonl and git-adds it; the file IS intended to be tracked. The previous 'Legacy files (from pre-Dolt versions)' comment is stale — the file is no longer legacy under the new auto-export workflow.

Do NOT commit .beads/issues.jsonl itself in this PR. The PR's only file changes are .jules/env_setup.sh and .beads/.gitignore. The JSONL will start being tracked in subsequent commits via the normal bd write cycle.

## Path allowlist (overrides the package scope rule for this tooling bead)

git add allowed only for:
  - .jules/env_setup.sh
  - .beads/.gitignore

If git status --porcelain shows any other path, abort with <!-- delegate-blocked -->. Do NOT git add .beads/issues.jsonl or any other file.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fresh Jules sandbox runs .jules/env_setup.sh after this PR merges, when the script completes, then neither the '/app/.beads has permissions 0775' warning nor the 'auto-export: git add failed' warning appears in the output

# Task: UI Polish - BOM Panel Styling

## Context
The `BOMPanel.tsx` component is functional but lacks visual polish. It needs to align with our production-grade design standards while accurately reflecting real-time constraints and totals.

- Refine the styling of the `BOMPanel` using Tailwind CSS.
- Ensure it displays clear totals for price, bin count, and area.
- Add unit tests for the component to handle edge cases:
  - Empty bin list.
  - Bins with missing prices.
  - Exceeding assembly-level budget caps.

## Links
- Component: `apps/web/src/ui/BOMPanel.tsx`
- State: `packages/store/src/useStore.ts`
- Design Guidelines: `.jules/product-guidelines.md`

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Responsive layout confirmed.
- [ ] Unit tests passing in `apps/web/src/ui/BOMPanel.test.tsx`.
acceptance_criteria: BOMPanel shows correct totals and handles empty state.

title: Spec alignment across all tools once realignment stabilizes
description:
Reframed after user feedback (2026-06-11): this is a retrospective-area topic, not an immediate AGENTS.md edit.

Two threads to figure out after the product-realignment work stabilizes:
1. Retrospective question: did we invest too heavily in planning tooling (OpenSpec + Beads + formulas + AGENTS.md rails) before having a product? Capture the honest answer in the product-realignment retrospective.
2. Goal: general spec alignment across ALL tools (Claude, Gemini, Jules, Opencode) — one source of truth that each tool consumes, instead of guidance drifting between AGENTS.md, OpenSpec, Beads memories, and per-tool configs.
